g.text: At the edge of a salt-worn town, Anya apprenticed under Mara, keeper of the harbor beacon.
Anya measured the oil. The old lamp burned long after the last boat reached shore.
For midsummer, Anya fitted a brighter mirror. It dazzled rooftops but made the beacon flicker.
Fog at the Breakwater | That Night
That night, fog erased the moon. A fishing boat drifted beyond the breakwater, searching for three steady sweeps.
Together they slowed the wheel, shaded the mirror, and restored the pause. Three beams crossed the fog.
At dawn, Anya rebuilt the shutter and marked the oil reserve. Every piece had one job; every turn, its time.
The boat answered with a deck lamp, found the channel, and returned safely. The harbor heard ropes and relieved laughter.
A Light That Returns | Years Later
Years later, Anya taught the pattern to a new keeper. The beacon didn't need to be the brightest light in the world.
